opex.notes: Footnote: "Expenses include VAT at 5% (not recoverable)." Chiller (Empower) is paid by tenants directly, so there is no district cooling line. The statement has no lines for common-area utilities, security/cleaning, or vacancy/collection loss.

discrepancies.title: OM yield 6.8% is on asking price, before 6.2% acquisition costs

sources.label: acquisition costs (DLD 4%, broker, trustee, mortgage registration)

discrepancies.why: A buyer pays AED 8,134,523 on top of the price. On price plus costs the same income gives 6.4%.

impact.basis: OM income on price plus acquisition costs, minus the stated yield

discrepancies.analyst_action: Compare deals on yield on total cost; ask the broker to restate the yield on that basis.

discrepancies.title: Cover calls the building 'fully tenanted' while the OM itself says 96% occupied
discrepancies.why: The cover headline says fully tenanted. Page 2 gives 96% occupancy. The rent roll shows 4 vacant units of 96 (92 let) and some units under renewal or notice. The headline overstates letting, so a buyer should rely on the dated rent roll rather than the marketing wording.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask the broker to confirm occupancy on a dated Ejari-backed rent roll. Reconcile the 'fully tenanted' claim to the 4 vacant units and to the units under renewal or with notice served.

notices.text: Tenants' security deposits of AED 431,225 transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
Cheque profile: 45% of rent on 1-2 cheques, 43% of rent on 3-4 cheques, 12% of rent on 6 or more cheques. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.

diligence_checklist.text: Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold status, single title, and that the buyer is eligible to own the plot.
Building completion certificate (Dubai Municipality) for the as-built building.
Affection plan and permitted use: confirm residential use and the plot's permitted floors match the building.
Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
Civil Defence completion and annual fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.
Owners' association: service charge budget, arrears and Mollak status for every unit.

rejected_model_findings.title: OM describes 96 individual title deeds and an owners association, not a single freehold title

evidence.quote: Individual title deeds allow flexible exit - sell in bulk or unit by unit
Building managed by a RERA-registered owners association; service charges paid through Mollak.

rejected_model_findings.why: The OM states freehold but also says there are 96 separate title deeds, that the building can be sold unit by unit, and that it is run by an owners association with service charges paid through Mollak. That points to a strata or unit-by-unit title structure rather than one title deed for the whole building. If so, the buyer would need to acquire and hold 96 deeds, and the owners association may control common areas, charges and voting. This affects deal structure, transfer costs and exit.
rejected_model_findings.analyst_action: Request the title deed(s) and Dubai Land Department title search for plot 366-0754. Confirm whether there is one deed or 96. Obtain the owners association constitution, Mollak statements and any service-charge arrears. Refer to legal counsel to confirm the ownership structure and what the seller can transfer in one sale.
rejected_model_findings.rejected_because: the OM states freehold tenure (verified) and no quoted evidence names a tenure or eligibility restriction; strata ownership is tested by the mandate's title filter

rejected_model_findings.title: Headline annual rent appears to include vacant units at potential rent
rejected_model_findings.why: The OM shows AED 8.93m as annual rental income and a 6.79% ROI built on it. The rent roll shows 4 of 96 units vacant, yet the code-computed in-place rent equals the potential rent (8,927,500). That suggests the headline figure counts vacant units at asking or projected rent, not contracted rent. The OM does not describe the figure as potential. If so, the in-place income and the yield are overstated.
rejected_model_findings.analyst_action: Rebuild in-place rent from let units only, using Ejari contracts. Compare it with the AED 8.93m headline and the owner statement rental income line. Recalculate yield on contracted income.
rejected_model_findings.rejected_because: contradicted by the rent roll: OM income AED 8,930,000 equals in-place rent AED 8,927,500 within 2%

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Decline**: the building is freehold strata title, and the mandate hard filter requires freehold single title.

Every other hard filter passes: asset type, area, unit count, price band, building age and no related-party master lease. No walk-away price or buy recommendation is given. Returns below are context only.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Aurelia Bay Tower, Business Bay, 96 units [[om.unit_count]], completed 2017 [[deal.completion_year]].
- **Price:** asking AED 131.5m [[deal.asking_price_aed]], which is AED 1,717 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_nsa]] on NSA. The OM's AED 1,099 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_bua]] is on BUA.
- **Income:** in-place rent AED 8.9m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] from direct leases, with no master tenant. Occupancy is 96% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] by units: 92 let [[rr.let_units]] and 4 vacant [[rr.vacant_units]]. The largest three-month expiry window holds 31% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]] of rent.

## Returns
For reference only; not decisive. These rest on the firm's house view, not on market evidence for this building.

| Metric | Result | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Unlevered IRR (pre-tax) | 1.0% [[uw.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]] | 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] |
| Unlevered equity multiple (pre-tax) | 1.05x [[uw.unlevered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] | 1.30x [[mandate.target_unlevered_equity_multiple.threshold]] |
| Going-in net yield on total cost | 4.7% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | 6.0% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] |
| Entry yield on price | 5.0% [[uw.entry_yield_on_price]] | none |
| Exit yield | 6.2% [[uw.exit_yield]] | none |

Year-1 NOI is AED 6.6m [[uw.noi_year1]]. Each return metric with a mandate threshold misses it.

Levered returns are secondary. Levered IRR is a loss of 1.6% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]] a year, the levered multiple is 0.92x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]], and Year-1 DSCR is 1.40x [[uw.dscr_year1]].

The OM's headline yield is 6.8% [[om.yield_stated]], on asking price with no income basis stated. On the buyer's basis (Year-1 NOI on price plus acquisition costs) it is 4.7% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]]. The gap is negative: the buyer's yield is 2.1 points [[uw.om_yield.gap_vs_stated]] lower than the OM's.

## What would make it fail
It fails on title before any return question. Returns are also far under target: the base case sits well below the 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] unlevered IRR target.

## Discrepancies
Both items are medium severity. Any lower-severity items are not discussed.

1. **OM yield ignores acquisition costs.** The OM's 6.8% [[om.yield_stated]] is on asking price, before acquisition costs of 6.2% [[uw.acquisition_costs_pct_of_price]] of price. The screen relied on its own engine. On price plus costs, the OM's own income gives 6.4% [[uw.om_yield.stated_income_on_total_cost]], 0.4 points [[disc.yield_excludes_acquisition_costs.impact_ratio]] lower. The buyer's NOI is lower again (see Returns). Treat this as one gap, not two.
2. **"Fully tenanted" cover claim.** The OM's own occupancy figure is 96% [[om.occupancy_stated]], which contradicts the cover headline. The rent roll shows 4 vacant units [[rr.vacant_units]] and some units under renewal or on notice. The screen relied on the dated rent roll. The headline overstates letting.

## Checks before diligence
Only if the committee revisits the mandate fit:
- Ask the broker to restate the yield on total cost. Compare deals on that basis.
- Get a dated, Ejari-backed rent roll. Reconcile "fully tenanted" to the vacant units and to the units under renewal or on notice.
- Tenant security deposits of AED 431k [[rr.deposits_aed]] transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
- Review the cheque profile. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.
- Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold status, single title, buyer eligibility.
- Dubai Municipality building completion certificate.
- Affection plan and permitted use.
- Ejari export for every lease, reconciled unit by unit.
- Civil Defence and fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.
- Owners' association service charge budget, arrears and Mollak status.

## Assumptions
House view: exit yield 6.2% [[uw.exit_yield]] over a 5-year [[uw.hold_years]] hold. Market rent falls 3.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1 and 1.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year2]] in Year 2, then grows 2.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]]. Structural vacancy is 5.0% [[assume.structural_vacancy]] and collection loss is 1.0% [[assume.collection_loss]]. Debt is sized to 1.40x [[assume.sizing_dscr]] cover on Year-1 NOI, giving a 33% [[uw.ltv]] loan to value at a 6.8% [[uw.interest_rate]] rate. The operating statement lacked common utilities and security and cleaning, so mandate defaults apply: AED 153k [[uw.opex_default.utilities_common]] and AED 230k [[uw.opex_default.security_cleaning]].
